name: The pronoun of separation (faṣl, ʿimād)
definition: A detached pronoun of rafʿ set between the subject and a definite predicate, to show that what follows is the predicate and not an adjective; the Basrans call it faṣl, the Kufans ʿimād, 'support'.
body: In zaydun huwa al-qāʾimu the pronoun huwa keeps al-qāʾimu from being read as an adjective of zaydun, and adds emphasis: 'Zayd is the one standing'. The Basrans held that it has no place in iʿrāb at all (lā maḥall lahu); the Kufans gave it a place, in the case of what came before or after it, and al-Inṣāf records the question. In al-Zubaydī's account of the masʾala zunbūriyya, a note explains al-Kisāʾī's answer fa-idhā huwa iyyāhā in these terms: he took huwa as an ʿimād and put what follows it in naṣb.
The standard example of the handbooks is a verse of the Qurʾān, where the pronoun stands between kunta and its predicate.

examples.text: Q 5:117: anta is the pronoun of separation between kāna's subject and its predicate al-raqība.
